body:
P9a: custom web address in Settings, checked until live (#599)

* Let an operator move the site to its own domain from the admin

ADR 0007 §8 makes a custom web address an optional upgrade with a
guided, checked step, so a client never edits DNS blind. The function
asks Firebase Hosting for the domain and shows the exact records Hosting
wants, then checks until the domain is live and adds it to sign-in.

The switch of EVENT_PUBLIC_URL stays a deploy: it is a deploy-time value
read across functions and the build, and changing it at runtime would
split the site between two addresses. Until the provisioner's GitHub App
exists, the hosting team runs that deploy; the page says so.

The custom sender domain is left for the console. Verifying a domain in
Postmark needs the account-level token, and ADR 0004's isolation rule
keeps account-wide credentials out of client projects.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_018gBJRkNQJGcw4SNsJ7AzQa
Signed-off-by: Joe Amditis <6799804+jamditis@users.noreply.github.com>

* Show every DNS change, survive slow and repeated adds, and keep checks honest

Codex on #599, each traced against the Hosting v1beta1 API:

- Hosting also asks for conflicting records to be removed. Showing only
  additions could leave a client stuck with nothing left to do on the
  page, so removals are listed and marked.
- Creating a domain is a long-running operation. Reading it at once
  could fail and lose the record, so a domain not yet readable is saved
  with no records and the next check fills them in.
- A domain Hosting already has is reused, and one removed within its
  30-day retention is restored with :undelete, so "you can add it again"
  holds.
- The functions never received EVENT_HOSTING_SITE, so a client whose
  site differs from the project ID targeted the wrong site. Both env
  writers pass it now.
- The hourly check skipped the historical-demo write policy and could
  change sign-in settings on a read-only demo.
- A check still waiting on Hosting could write a removed domain back. It
  now writes only if the record is still the one it started from.

Signed-off-by: Joe Amditis <6799804+jamditis@users.noreply.github.com>
